cohort: Healthy mothers and their primary infants delivering at Richmond University Medical Center on Staten Island, N.Y. between January 2012 and January 2019.
finding: The study concluded that the overall risk-benefit ratio for both maternal and neonatal outcomes was equal between trial of labor and cesarean delivery on maternal request, supporting no bias for either mode of delivery.
mod_finding: Trial of labor was associated with shorter NICU stays but increased maternal fever, lacerations, and episiotomies, while cesarean delivery on maternal request was linked to longer NICU stays but shorter maternal hospital stays and less maternal fever.
